svg.text: Three measurements on three different clocks — and three independent ways for a name to be refused. Every threshold below is the one in the code.
1 · THE SHAPE — what the daily screen is looking for
150-day line, rising — the trend gate that is never waived
prior high — the highest close of the last 200 sessions, last 10 excluded · ±3% either side of it = AT-BREAKOUT · more than 3% past it = EXTENDED>BREAK
the 20-day range — measured, then ranked against this name's own year
③ the coil — this is the heartbeat
④ the break, on 2× the 60-day volume
volume drying up inside the box is a condition, not a nicety: a range this tight on rising volume is a fight, not an accumulation
where that sits among up to 253 rolling 20-day ranges drawn from
bottom quartile of its own year
and tight in absolute terms too
Under 160 sessions of history the primary line falls back to 50-day and the
row is marked 50d* — reported, never quietly dropped.
A fixed “20-day range ≤ 7%” only ever fires on ETFs and staples. A
high-beta name coils tightly by its own standards and never by anyone
else's — so the bar is a percentile.
0.4×3m + 0.3×6m + 0.3×12m excess return over SPY (USD) or ISF.L
its percentile across the core universe — speculatives excluded, and
they can never be RS-LEADER. ≥ 80 fires it.
20-day up-day volume ÷ down-day volume. Above 1 = net
biggest bar in the last 5 sessions ÷ the 60-day average, tagged with
that day's direction. ≥ 2.0 → VOL-2X-UP or VOL-2X-DOWN.
plain session returns. They drive nothing on their own: the
sector-pressure table aggregates them and emits no tag.
Direction is the whole of it. A 2× volume bar on a down day is
distribution, and a magnitude-only read files it as a buy signal — which
is why acc is measured separately, over 20 days.
Composite score /100, five pillar sub-scores, and the ACCEL / RECORD tags
IS ANY OF IT ALREADY IN THE PRICE?
The other half, and deliberately a separate test: growth you can still be paid
One exception, and only one: a fresh volume breakout above a completed
base may enter at a new high.
Record earnings with nothing left to pay for them is the commonest
failure on record: 18 of the 40 check-failures in the ledger are gate 6,
GATE CARD — 7 checks for a stock, 8 for an ETF
None of the three can outvote another. A name can be maximally coiled, top-decile momentum and posting record earnings — and still be refused on headroom alone.
